conviction_note: Nothing found that the market has not seen: Q3 consensus revenue ($3.36B, ~+7.7% y/y) sits in the middle of the company's own high-single-digit guide, Wayfair has beaten revenue consensus in recent prints (Q2 $3.52B vs $3.47B), and the only fresh outside evidence is a soft September furniture category in card data (NRF -2.7% y/y) and a Prime Day shift that Amazon flagged; the stock trades on the Q4 guide and the acceleration narrative, which no source here predicts, so p_up sits at 49 on a move scale of ~13.5 (implied 12.84, median past reaction 12.75); the findings sum to -0.4 and the scaled number to -0.27, they agree.
bar: Q3 2026 revenue $3.36B and adjusted EPS $0.84 (whisper $0.87), Earnings Whispers https://beta.earningswhispers.com/go/x/W (fetched 2026-11-03); company guide on the Q2 call 2026-08-04: high-single-digit revenue growth, gross margin 29.5-30.5% at the low end, advertising 10.5-11.5% at the low end, adj. EBITDA margin 6-7%, weighted shares ~137M, https://s24.q4cdn.com/589059658/files/doc_earnings/2026/q2/transcript/CORRECTED-TRANSCRIPT_Wayfair-Inc-W-US-Q2-2026-Earnings-Call.pdf. On Q3 2025 revenue of ~$3.12B, HSD growth is ~$3.34-3.40B, so the revenue bar is consistent with the guide. The EPS bar is disputed: an older Zacks figure of $0.17 (likely stale or GAAP) disagrees with $0.84, so nothing here is sized on EPS.
positioning_check: Short interest 10.68M shares, 9.92% of float, 5.3 days to cover as of the 2026-10-15 settlement (FINRA, published 2026-10-26), down 10.7% from 11.95M on 2026-09-30: https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NYSE/W/short-interest/. Elevated but not crowded, and shorts were covering into the print. Options: event-implied move 12.84%, 25d skew +0.22 vol points (balanced), put/call OI 1.06 (sealed baseline). Stock $111.13, 7.5% below its 52-week high, +93.6% off the low, 20d run-up +5.4%, 5d -1.6%; beta ~3 (MarketBeat 2026-10-08).

findings.finding: Management guided Q3 2026 to high-single-digit revenue growth, above its old mid-single-digit guides, and said growth would keep accelerating ('5% to 10% to 15% to 20%'). Consensus $3.36B (~+7.7% on Q3 2025's ~$3.12B) sits in the middle of that range. Wayfair has beaten revenue consensus in recent prints: Q2 2026 $3.52B vs $3.47B expected (+1.4%), adj. EPS $0.95 vs $0.90. So a small revenue beat is likely, but it lands inside what the company guided.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 (2026-08-04) beat revenue by 1.4% and EPS by $0.05: +29.97%. Q3 2025 (2025-10-28) beat: +23.22%. Q1 2026 (2026-04-30): -12.75%. Q4 2025 (2026-02-19): -13.02%. Sealed baseline. Beats have been bought hard when the forward narrative held and sold hard when it did not, so the reported quarter alone does not set the sign.
findings.why_not_priced: It is mostly priced: consensus already sits at the guide midpoint and the whisper ($0.87) is above consensus ($0.84). The small residual is the habit of beating. If the market expected a large upside surprise, the whisper and consensus would sit at the top of the HSD range (~$3.40B), not the middle.
findings.independence: Q2 beat figures from a different source: https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/analyst-wayfair-nyse-w-price-target-raised-to-11700-2026-10-08/ ; Q2 8-K exhibit https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001616707/000161670726000147/a2026-08x04ex991.htm (same company, a different document).

findings.finding: The CNBC/NRF Retail Monitor (card data from ~120M cards), released 2026-10-08, had furniture and home furnishings down 2.7% y/y in September 2026, the only category that fell, while total retail rose ~4% y/y. In July 2026 the same category was +2.71% y/y. That points to the home category weakening through the quarter. Wayfair's guide assumed flat macro ('bouncing along the bottom') and share gains.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No resolved case in the baseline of a macro category print leading Wayfair's own revenue. Wayfair has grown through flat-to-down category data in 2025-26 on claimed share gains (Q2 2026 US +8.7%).
findings.why_not_priced: It is a proxy, not company data: the category counts store-based furniture retailers (with their own online sales), not nonstore pure plays like Wayfair. The new methodology also breaks comparison with earlier months, so July and September are not on the same basis. It is public, but analysts have not cut Q3 revenue below the guide midpoint, so it has not reached consensus. If it had been priced, consensus would sit at the low end of HSD (~$3.34B) and the 20d run-up would not be +5.4%.
findings.independence: Proxy only. July's +2.71% comes from a different NRF release: https://nrf.com/media-center/press-releases/cnbc-nrf-retail-monitor-shows-10th-month-of-sales-growth-in-july. No company or counterparty confirmation.

findings.finding: Amazon's Q3 2026 online stores sales grew only ~2% y/y ($68.47B vs $67.41B), about +6% adjusting for Prime Day moving from July 2025 (Q3) into Q2 2026. That leaves Wayfair facing a July 2025 comp that an analyst on the Q2 call called 'a really tough comp in July', with no Prime Day halo or competing event in July 2026. Management guided HSD knowing the calendar.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None on record for a peer calendar shift.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced and inside the guide: Wayfair knew the July comp when it guided on 2026-08-04. The sign is ambiguous, because less Prime Day competition in July could also help. If the shift were a known Wayfair headwind, consensus would sit below the HSD midpoint.
findings.independence: Amazon's own release: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001018724/000101872426000038/amzn-20260930xex991.htm ; the tough-July-comp remark is in the Q2 transcript (different document).

findings.finding: The Q4 guide is the line the stock will trade on, and management set a high bar on 2026-08-04: 'you're going to see accelerating revenue growth', with a path to 10%, 15% and 20%. Way Day ran 2026-10-24 to 26, inside Q4, so quarter-to-date commentary will be read against that promise while the September category data (finding 2) points softer. A Q4 guide of merely HSD would read as a stall.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 2025 introduced an acceleration guide and the stock rose 23.22%; Q2 2026 raised to an HSD guide and it rose 29.97%; the two prints that fell ~13% (Feb and Apr 2026) were the ones where the guide did not extend the story (sealed baseline; the causes of those two are not sourced here).
findings.why_not_priced: It is an inference about the bar the narrative sets, not a number. The balanced skew (+0.22) says the option market has no view on the direction of the guide. If a stall were expected, puts would be bid and the stock would not sit 7.5% from its high.
findings.independence: Way Day dates: https://www.autobound.ai/companies/wayfair/news (dates as reported in a search snippet). Shares the Q2 transcript with finding 1; this one is on the forward guide, not the reported quarter.

findings.finding: Positioning: short interest fell 10.7% to 10.68M shares (9.92% of float, 5.3 days to cover) at the 2026-10-15 settlement, from 11.95M on 2026-09-30, and was 14.9M (13.8%) on 2026-06-30. Shorts are steadily covering but still about 10% of float, on a beta-3 stock with balanced skew.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The two largest positive reactions (+23%, +30%) came with double-digit short interest. Short float has been falling since mid-2026.
findings.why_not_priced: The squeeze is a mechanism on any beat, not a priced level. Covering means less fuel than in August, so the size is small.
findings.independence: Sept 30 figure 11.95M, 4.8 days to cover: https://massive.com/quote/w ; June 30 14.9M: https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NASDAQ/W/short-interest/

findings.finding: Management said on the Q2 call that it had 'largely finished repurchasing' its convertible bonds and would stop booking extinguishment losses (Q2 2026 loss $59M; $102M year to date). That should 'structurally boost' GAAP net income. Q2 GAAP net loss was only $1M, so Q3 could show a clearly positive GAAP profit headline. Weighted shares rise to ~137M on the 2028 notes redemption.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None on record; below-the-line items have not driven this name's reactions.
findings.why_not_priced: It is a headline-optics item below operating income, mostly known. The stray $0.17 Zacks EPS estimate may be a GAAP number that a GAAP profit would clear, but that is speculative. Sized as a one-off fraction.
findings.independence: Q2 8-K: $59M loss on extinguishment, long-term debt down to $2,797M: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001616707/000161670726000147/a2026-08x04ex991.htm (same company, different document).

findings.finding: Insiders sold 296,024 shares (~$30.6M) in the 90 days to early October. CEO Niraj Shah sold 69,000 shares on 2026-09-14 at $103.35 (19% of his directly reported holding) under a 10b5-1 plan, and a director and an officer also sold.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Founder selling under 10b5-1 plans is routine at Wayfair; no reaction is attributable to it.
findings.why_not_priced: These sales are public Form 4s on a prearranged plan, so they carry little information. Filed for completeness.

findings.finding: Baird raised its target to $117 from $116 on 2026-10-08 and kept Neutral, against a consensus target of ~$121 and a Moderate Buy rating. The sell side has made no recent move into the print.
findings.why_not_priced: This is wire copy and fully priced. It is filed only to show the bar was not moved in October.

baseline_tension: Neither side: the skew is balanced (+0.22), the run-up modest (+5.4% over 20 days), short interest elevated but falling, and the only fresh outside evidence (soft September furniture category, Amazon's Prime Day shift) is proxy-level and partly offset by Wayfair's record of beating a midpoint consensus. Nothing here argues the option market is mispricing the direction.
lessons_applied: Lesson 5 (a narrow proxy is filed small): the NRF September furniture category finding went from -1.0 to -0.8, because it does not measure nonstore sellers and its methodology break makes July and September incomparable
'Asking what the market missed generates pessimism' plus lesson 3: the Q4-guide finding is an inference about the bar, so it went from -0.5 to -0.3; p_up moved from 48 to 49
Lesson 6: the EPS bar is disputed ($0.84 vs $0.17), so no finding is sized on EPS; the revenue bar agrees with the company guide and stands
Lesson 7: short interest was checked before the negatives (9.9% float, 5.3 days to cover, falling); not crowded enough to resize the negatives further
Left standing: the reported-quarter beat finding (+0.5, inside the guide), the one-off GAAP item (+0.3, already sized as a fraction), positioning (+0.3), insider selling (-0.1), Baird (0)
